speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've been experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; please tell me, when did these symptoms start, and has the pain radiated to your arm, jaw, or back?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture)

The history of forceful vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption, followed by sudden chest pain and choking, is highly specific for an esophageal tear. Given the severity of these symptoms, I am requesting immediate confirmation. REQUEST TEST: Chest X-Ray; REQUEST IMAGES: Thoracic CT scan with contrast.
